en: The Philippine flag features a sun with eight rays, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a Senate with 24 members and a House of Representatives with over 300 district lawmakers.
The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, ending exactly 333 years of Spanish colonial administration that began in 1565.
While the Philippines has over 180 distinct native languages, the 1987 Constitution designates only Filipino and English as the two official languages.
The massive Sinulog Festival in Cebu attracts over two million attendees annually to watch the traditional two-step forward, one-step backward dance.
The Lumad people of Mindanao consist of at least 18 distinct ethnolinguistic groups, making up one of the largest indigenous populations in the country.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, stands about one meter tall and possesses a massive wingspan measuring up to two meters across.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first Asian to enter Harvard Medical School and founded a pediatric hospital in Manila at age 26.
Jose Rizal wrote his groundbreaking novel Noli Me Tangere at age 26, but was tragically executed by the Spanish government just nine years later.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote for the president, vice president, and 24 senators in national elections held every six years.
The traditional Bayanihan spirit is historically symbolized by a community of roughly 20 men carrying an entire nipa hut on bamboo poles.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva, known as the Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture, created more than 100 major sculptures during his six-decade artistic career.
